subject: Action: collect Neurolytics prompts for eval + baseline model recommendations
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>
To: Ariane Dupree <ariane.dupre@neurolytics.ai>, Ben Cho <ben.cho@neurolytics.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Action: collect Neurolytics prompts for eval + baseline model recommendations

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great conversation and clear product alignment. Per our call, I wanted to capture the concrete next steps for the prompt/quality evaluation so we can move to a scoped benchmark quickly.

Recap / asks for your team (Neurolytics):
- Share a representative sample of end-user prompts (CSV preferred). Include the prompt text, any system/context, and a short label for the expected intent/category. If you can't share raw PHI, provide redacted versions + a few synthetic PHI examples labeled clearly.
- Highlight 8–12 edge cases or failure modes you’re most worried about (examples where current models hallucinate or redact incorrectly).
- Provide simple pass/fail criteria for high-risk flows (e.g., legal extract accuracy >= 85% exact-match; hallucination rate < 2% for regulatory answers).
- Usage profile: typical prompt length, concurrency targets, and SLOs (p95 latency target).

What Redwood will do after we receive the sample:
- Run a baseline eval across two candidate families: (1) lightweight low-latency quantized model (7B-class) and (2) higher-capacity accuracy-first model (13B-class). See the benchmark templates: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Neurolytics-Evals-Shared
- Measure: exact-match / F1 for extraction, ROUGE-L for summarization, hallucination rate, and latency at 512 tokens.
- Produce an evaluation report with suggested model/config (quantization, batch size, cache policy) and cost/latency tradeoffs.

Timeline proposal:
- July 23: Neurolytics shares prompt sample + redaction guidance
- July 24–28: Redwood runs evals and internal QA
- July 29: Deliver evaluation report & suggested rollout plan (canary, A/B)

Please reply to confirm this timeline and attach the CSV when ready. If redaction/PHI is a blocker we'll accept masked records and a short compliance contact to sign an MSA addendum.

Thanks — I’ve cc’d Monica (SE) to own the eval run and Markus (AEs lead) for any commercial questions.

—
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com | +1 415-555-0123
Redwood Inference

P.S. Attached is a lightweight eval plan draft (eval-plan-neurolytics.md) for your review.
From: Ariane Dupree <ariane.dupre@neurolytics.ai>

Cc: Ben Cho <ben.cho@neurolytics.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 17:02:41 -0700
Subject: Re: Action: collect Neurolytics prompts for eval + baseline model recommendations

Thanks Jordan — appreciate the clear plan. I attached a CSV with ~200 anonymized prompts and our redaction policy. A few important notes up front:
- We cannot share raw PHI outside approved processors. The CSV is redacted; we also included a small encrypted sample (5 records) containing PHI that we can share under a DPA addendum.
- Primary categories in the sample: customer_support, legal_extract, clinical_notes.
- Our compliance contact is procurement@neurolytics.ai for DPA / MSA addendum coordination.

Attached: neurolytics_prompts_sample.csv (CSV, 120KB); neurolytics_redaction_policy.pdf (PDF, 85KB)

Let us know if the sanitized sample is enough for your metrics or if you need a PHI-containing sample under a controlled transfer.

Best,
Ariane
Head of Product Research | Neurolytics
ariane.dupre@neurolytics.ai

Nice recap — quick SE notes from my side before we start the eval run:
- Candidate baseline models I recommend we test (config + reasons):
  * rw-7b-q4f (low-latency, good for short Q&A/CS flows)
  * rw-13b-8q (higher-capacity, better for legal_extract and long-context summarization)
- Metrics: exact-match / F1 for extraction, ROUGE-L for summarization, hallucination rate (manually sampled), and p95 token latency at 512 input tokens.
- For PHI cases: we'll run a masked-PHI experiment where we replace PHI tokens with tags and measure extraction fidelity separately. If they provide a small PHI sample under DPA we can run a direct evaluation.
- Ops ask: need HubSpot record to attach artifacts (HubSpot:HS-98321) and a shared folder for outputs (Drive link in the thread).

I'll spin up the eval runners when we have the CSV. Jordan — I can also draft a short de-id checklist to return to Neurolytics if they want guidance on redaction best practices.
